sections.overview: Eidolon dupreanum is a large fruit bat endemic to Madagascar and assessed as Vulnerable. It is a congener of the African straw-coloured fruit bat E. helvum; see that profile for its widespread continental relative.
sections.identification: Regional accounts describe a large pteropodid with reported body mass around 250–340 g; they provide fewer field marks than measurements.
sections.habitat: It occurs on Madagascar and has been documented roosting in caves, rocky cliffs and, occasionally, dense tree foliage.
sections.diet: A study in eastern Madagascar found a diet composed mainly of fruit, with Eucalyptus flowers also consumed.
sections.behavior: Researchers identify it as cave-dwelling and capture it at cave mouths around dusk and dawn; detailed movement data remain limited.
sections.reproduction: Field monitoring recorded lactating females in November and December and estimated annual female fecundity at about 0.23 young per female.
sections.ecology: By eating fruit, it moves seeds between feeding and roosting sites; the diet study also found some evidence that gut passage can improve seed germination.
sections.conservation: The global assessment is Vulnerable. Surveys in northern Madagascar associated recent hunting evidence at roosts with declines in a monitored colony, while emphasizing cave disturbance risks.
